title: Top AnswerConnect alternatives in 2026
summary: There are dozens of AnswerConnect alternatives on the market. How do you choose the best one? Explore the seven best options + features and pricing.
body_markdown:
AnswerConnect is a 24/7 live answering service for small to medium-sized businesses. While it’s been around for more than 25 years, it may not be the perfect fit for *your* business.


Past users say it has downsides, like long setup times and inconsistent experiences with agents. Since AnswerConnect uses 100% human receptionists, it costs more in time and training than using AI receptionists. So the pricing may not scale as your business grows.


This article covers the best AnswerConnect alternatives on the market. You’ll learn about their pros and cons and how much they cost. We’ll also explore additional limitations of AnswerConnect that push users to seek other solutions.


The top AnswerConnect alternatives in 2026 are:


- **Quo’s Sona:** Best alternative for growing businesses


- **Smith.ai:** Best alternative for call centers with a layer of AI


- **Ooma AI receptionist:** Best alternative for callers in Mexico and Puerto Rico


- **Ruby:** Best alternative for high-touch live answering


- **Abby Connect:** Best alternative for flexible receptionist plans


- **PATLive:** Best alternative for emergency dispatch and call overflows


- **3CX AI receptionist:** Best alternative for multi-language support


##


**Comparing AnswerConnect alternatives**


Here’s how the best AnswerConnect alternatives line up side by side:

Let’s start with one of the highest-rated options on G2.


### **1. Quo: The top AnswerConnect alternative for growing businesses**


#### Pros


- 24/7 AI receptionist powered by SonaSona is included in all Quo plans
- Customizable call flow
- Automatic call logging
- Sona is priced per call
- Integrations with Zoho CRM and other CRMs


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. Companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a business phone that combines calls, texts, and AI capabilities in one platform. It includes[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s built-in AI receptionist, which can answer calls with 24/7 coverage so you never miss a customer again. That way, all your phone communication is in a single place.


Sona is fully customizable to your business. It can route calls, answer customer questions, and capture leads over text. Just use the three-step setup wizard to get started.


You can customize *how* and *when* Sona takes calls using a simple drag-and-drop call flow builder. It’s easy to learn, yet still lets you set up conditional logic. For example, you might set up Sona to only answer after-hours calls. Or you can have Sona answer as a fallback option when your reps can’t.


Plus, Sona comes with business-friendly pricing that’s transparent and practical for growing teams. Sona uses flat-rate per-call pricing rather than per-minute billing. That way, you only pay for call volume, not how long each call lasts.


Quo’s base plan includes 10 Sona calls for free, plus $1 per call if you go beyond the limit. But don’t worry: Quo disables overage charges by default to protect you from surprise costs. You can also purchase additional Sona credits if you need to scale your Sona usage as demand increases.


If leads text you, Sona for lead capture can capture their information for your team to follow up and answer repetitive questions.


Rohan Aurora, owner of Altitude Cleaning Crew, said:


*“We’re in the trust business. Auto-replies end conversations. Sona starts them. It keeps customers engaged until my team can step in, captures every lead after hours, and lets us follow up already knowing exactly what the customer needs. Our customers are happy texting with Sona, and we no longer hear, ‘Can I talk to a human?’ That’s a huge win.”*


But Sona is just one part of Quo. It works alongside Quo’s business phone features to help you build better customer relationships and save time for other tasks. For example, you’ll be able to split responsibility for incoming calls and texts via shared numbers. Every conversation thread lets you easily see who said what, including calls handled by Sona. You can delegate tasks using Quo Tasks. You can also use group messaging to chat about context as a team.


See why 90,000 businesses trust Quo to build stronger customer relationships with a[seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) . You can test speaking to Sona yourself during your trial.


#### **Key features of Quo**


- Lead capture through text
- AI personas that match your brand
- Customizable call routing
- Native CRM integrations
- Calendar integrations
- AI[call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording)
- AI call summaries


#### **Quo pricing**


[Quo pricing](https://www.quo.com/pricing) is transparent and fully accessible; no hidden fees, and our pricing isn’t locked behind a form. Our business phone plans are divided into three tiers:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada, voicemail, shared contacts, call notes, call recording, group messaging, and more
- **Business:** $23 per user per month for group calls, call transfers, shared phone numbers, Salesforce and HubSpot integrations, and more
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for AI call tags, inbound phone support, priority chat and email support, and dedicated onboarding


Each Quo plan comes with 10 free calls for our AI receptionist, Sona. If you need more than that, you can upgrade to one of our paid Sona plans:

### **2. Smith AI: Best for call centers with a layer of AI**


#### Pros


- AI and human receptionists
- Free AI receptionist plan
- Per-call pricing model


#### Cons


- Inconsistent agent performance
- No self-serve cancellation
- Billing and cancellation issues
- Add-ons are charged per call


[Smith.ai](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-alternatives/) is a call handling company that combines AI and live receptionists. You can purchase a 100% human service, 100% AI, or a mix of both. Pricing for AI-first plans is relatively straightforward and charges per call per month. But for human-first plans, you’ll have to purchase add-ons on top of the flat rate. For example:


- If a caller books an appointment, Smith.ai will charge an additional $1.50
- Activating call recordings and transcripts adds $0.25 to all calls
- Checking for conflicts on your calendar costs $0.50 each time


You’ll notice that some of these add-ons are based on what the agent does on the call. But nobody knows what a caller will ask for. This makes your costs hard to predict and control.


If you want the best of both worlds, you can switch to a hybrid plan. This mixes AnswerConnect’s live agents with AI tools to help with specific use cases. You might send new callers to human receptionists and recurring callers to AI for $2.50 per call. But hybrid pricing estimates start at 30 calls per month, so the least you would pay is $117 per month.


Smith.ai doesn’t have its own phone platform, so you’ll still need to sign up for a business phone plan if you don’t already have one. That’s an additional cost above what you’re paying for Smith.ai. But then your call records will be in two different systems. You’ll have to piece conversations together, which can be more time-consuming than it’s worth.


You should also know that past Smith.ai customers have experienced problems with its human and AI agents. For example, users report that human agents sometimes[don’t follow the script](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/680a97bc4f4ee3f34f8b40a6) :


*“The agents are so incompetent that they always fail to follow call handling instructions. They have extreme difficulty following even the most straightforward scripts. The agents intentionally make mistakes to boost follow up/ outward calls. I emailed Haley, the Client Support, but she procrastinated.*


AI agents seem to be[giving callers trouble](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a8382833a81521e70672548) , too:


*“I signed up for their service to create an AI receptionist to schedule callbacks. However, the AI receptionist was faulty and would repeatedly ask questions that were already answered by the client.”*


Not happy and want to cancel? Other reviewers[indicate](https://uk.trustpilot.com/reviews/6ac91975048491c89374b878) that cancellation requests take a long time to resolve.


*“I’ve been trying to cancel my account for over a week. They still haven’t done it, and I believe it’s because they want to make cancelling hard. That’s disingenuous, and not a good business practice.”*


### Key features of Smith.ai


**


- 24/7 availability
- Lead qualification
- Appointment booking
- Call summaries and transcripts
- CRM integrations
- Live transfer and handoff


### Smith.ai pricing


**


Smith.ai has three pricing plans:AI receptionists, human receptionists, and a hybrid solution.


Its AI-first pricing offers volume discounts for high call volumes. For example:


- **Free:** 25 free calls per month with 24/7 availability, lead qualification, call routing, AI scheduling, and native CRM integrations
- **Pro:** Starts at $150 per month for 75 calls, dedicated onboarding and setup, and custom SMS branding
- **Enterprise:** Starts at $500 per month for 300 calls, custom AI prompting, unlimited integrations and workflows, and a dedicated success manager


All human-first plans include lead qualification, new client intake, a dedicated phone number, and 24/ staffing. Additional services and features are charged per call. Here’s what to expect from the base prices:


- **Starter:** $300 a month for 30 calls, with an $11.50 overage fee per call over 30
- **Basic.** $810 a month for 90 calls, with a $10.50 overage fee per call over 90
- **Pro.** $2,100 a month for 300 calls, with an $8.50 overage fee per call over 300
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing based on your needs


Smith.ai’s hybrid plans range from $1.60 to $7 per call, depending on the complexity of your workflow. For this reason, you’ll need a custom quote. You can reach out to the sales team for more customized pricing.


### **3. Ooma: Best AnswerConnect alternative for callers in Mexico and Puerto Rico**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls to and from the US, Canada, Puerto Rico, and Mexico
- Texting in the US and Canada


#### Cons


- AI receptionist requires an add-on
- Per-license pricing


[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) is a business phone solution that recently released the Beta version of its AI Receptionist. You can use the platform itself to make and receive calls in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico. Its AI receptionist answers calls in English, French, and Spanish. Plus, users have the option of recording a greeting in whatever language they like.


Apart from languages, you can use Ooma’s AI receptionist to:


- Pick up calls 24/7
- Route calls
- Book appointments
- Handle complex inquiries, backed by an online knowledge base


The cost for the AI Receptionist starts at $49.99 per license per month. That’s more than the cost of an Ooma user license. And keep in mind this is in addition to what you’re already paying for Ooma.


### Key features of Ooma AI receptionist


**


- 24/7 availability
- Languages include English, Spanish, and French
- Unlimited calling to and from Mexico and Puerto Rico
- Lead capture
- Call routing
- Appointment booking


### Ooma AI receptionist pricing


**


There are four main[Ooma Office pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) plans.


- **Ooma Office Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico and a free toll-free number with 500 incoming call minutes
- **Ooma Office Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for 100 text messages, calling from the desktop app, and call recording
- **Ooma Office Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for 400 text messages, team chat, one-to-many messages, and CRM integrations
- **Ooma Office Enterprise:** Custom quote for a Microsoft Teams integration, advanced analytics, and custom implementations


Ooma’s AI Receptionist is an add-on that costs $49.99 per license per month. It comes with 100 free minutes of AI usage. After that, you’ll need to upgrade to a higher usage tier.


### **4. Ruby: Best for high-touch live answering service**


#### Pros


- HIPAA compliant
- Outbound call assistance
- 5,000+ integrations


#### Cons


- Very high cost
- Inconsistent service quality
- Billing issues


[Ruby](https://www.quo.com/blog/ruby-receptionist-alternatives/) is a human-first virtual receptionist service supported by AI-powered transcripts, sentiment analysis, and call flows for high-touch businesses. Its clients include professional services like legal, financial, healthcare, and home services.


Unlike other virtual receptionists on this list, Ruby provides outbound call assistance. For example, it can help you with payment collection services in addition to the usual lead capture and call forwarding tasks.


That said, Ruby has a reputation for being a “premium” service with higher prices than its competitors. You’re typically billed in 30-second increments, rounded up. You’re also billed for post-call wrap-up activities.


This high cost is made worse by surprise charges and overage bills. One reviewer’s bill jumped from $660 to $5,100 without any notice:


*“We were lied to by \[a\] salesperson…, who told us we would receive an alert if we were approaching our monthly minute limit. There was no alert, and what we expected would be a bill for $660.00 rose to $5,100.00 with no notice to us. It is no surprise that in 2021, Ruby was ordered to pay $12 million in damages as the result of a class action suit for deceptive billing. We cancelled our service after 1 month and asked for a refund, but our request was denied.”* —[Consumer Affairs](https://www.consumeraffairs.com/business/ruby-receptionists.html#:~:text=Walton%20Beach%2C%20FL-,Customer%20Service,Report,-Carmen)


Other customers have complained about negative experiences with agents. In one case, a receptionist was getting names wrong and letting[solicitors](https://www.g2.com/products/ruby-receptionists/reviews/ruby-receptionists-review-7667040) through. In another, the receptionist[misdirected calls](https://www.g2.com/products/ruby-receptionists/reviews/ruby-receptionists-review-8506422) and sent incorrect details.


Yet another customer[complained](https://www.g2.com/products/ruby-receptionists/reviews/ruby-receptionists-review-4746831) about discrepancies between calls logged and time billed. Even their Ruby agent mentioned it took them two years to learn how billing worked.


Keep in mind Ruby doesn’t have its own business phone. You’ll have to manually compare call records from two different platforms to get a complete customer interaction *and* pay for a business phone in addition to Ruby’s already-high pricing.


### Key features of Ruby


**


- 24/7 availability
- Lead qualification
- Call routing
- Outbound call assistance
- Payment collection
- AI sentiment analysis


### Ruby pricing


**


Ruby has four available plans, all with the same features. The only difference is the price and number of minutes. Here’s what you can expect to pay for each:


- **Startup:** $250 per month for 50 minutes per month
- **One-Person Business:** $395 per month for 100 minutes per month
- **Small Business:** $720 per month for 200 minutes per month
- **Large Business:** $1,725 per month for 500 minutes per month


### **5. Abby Connect: Best for backup human agents**


#### Pros


- Simple pricing
- No contract
- HIPAA compliance


#### Cons


- Billing issues
- Requires call forwarding
- Inconsistent agent performance


Abby Connect is a virtual answering service that offers human and AI receptionists, so you can mix and match them based on your preferences.


Billing is based on “Abby Minutes,” which function similarly to credits. Each plan gives you a certain number of Abby Minutes. One Abby Minute will buy you one minute from a human agent or two minutes from an AI agent. So if the Starter plan comes with 50 Abby Minutes, you get either 50 minutes for a human agent or 100 minutes for an AI agent.


Abby Connect doesn’t offer a built-in phone number. You’ll have to forward calls from your business phone system to the AI agent instead. This can make it hard to build a clear conversation history, since information is scattered across multiple tools.


Some customers report issues with Abby Connect’s billing and performance. One[reviewer](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/67eaa965098cd8cf207f47bb) was billed for spam calls, ring time, and a Google Calendar integration.


Performance may be inconsistent, too. Human agents may not always follow procedure and may put customers on hold for longer than necessary, according to a review on the[Better Business Bureau](https://www.bbb.org/us/nv/las-vegas/profile/answering-service/abby-connect-1086-81271/complaints) website:


*“We have been paying Abby Connect to answer our phone lines. Over the past few months, Abby Connect has failed to answer many of our calls, picked up our customers’ calls and then placed them on hold, and in an outrageous instance, told one of our customers to hold on because Abby Connect was overworked and had other more important callers to answer.”*


### Key features of Abby Connect


**


- Free trial
- No contract
- 24/7 service
- Choose from human, AI, or both
- Self-serve controls
- Abby Connect portal and app
- Call blocking
- Custom transfer music


### Abby Connect pricing


**


All Abby Connect plans include the same features. The biggest differences are the number of free minutes and the overage fees for each tier, although the overage fees aren’t publicly available.


Here’s what to expect on each plan:


- **Starter:** $165 a month for 50 Abby Minutes
- **Essential:** $329 a month for 100 Abby Minutes
- **Professional:** $599 a month for 200 Abby Minutes
- **Growth:** $1,380 a month for 500 Abby Minutes


### **6. PATLive: Best AnswerConnect alternative for emergencies**


#### Pros


- Call answering
- Outbound calls
- Chat support
- Overflow call handling
- Emergency dispatch


#### Cons


- Inconsistent agent performance
- Billing errors
- Long hold times


PATLive is a 24/7 answering service that uses 100% US-based human receptionists. In addition to law firms and home service companies, it works with government agencies, nonprofits, and IT companies.


PATLive’s biggest claim to fame is emergency dispatch services. Callers who need something right away, even after hours, can get an immediate response. The receptionists can also talk to customers via live chat and make outbound calls on your behalf. Is your in-house team overwhelmed with calls? The company can provide call overflow handling services.


Unfortunately, some PATLive customers have had bad experiences.[One customer wrote](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/5fd797bf755dc10b482266bc) that their PATLive agent sent them misspelled names, emails, and addresses. They also mentioned their monthly bills were up to 10 times what they expected.


Another reviewer said that their callers get put on hold for too long, leading to abandoned calls that still have to be paid for. See for yourself:


*“Phone calls are put on music hold for a while before anyone live answers; a lot of callers hang up during this time, and we get charged for it. Oftentimes, the receptionist can’t understand the caller, and the caller gets frustrated having to repeat themselves. The receptionists keep calling us by the wrong name.”* —[Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/5fe114f8755dc107e0cadad2)


### Key features of PATLive


**


- US-based receptionists
- 24/7 availability
- Message-taking
- Lead collection
- Overflow call handling
- Sales support
- Event registrations
- Emergency dispatch
- Call screening and transfers


### PATLive pricing


**


PATLive has three types of pricing plans based on the caller interaction. You can choose from Call Answering, Outbound Calls, or Live Chat tiers.


Here’s what to expect from each.


With their Live Call Answering plans, you’ll get human agents who are available 24/7 for lead capture, call transfer, and other services. Tiers are defined based on the minutes you buy:


- **Pay as you go:** $49 per month, plus $2.99 per extra minute
- **50 minutes:** $99 per month, plus $2.29 per extra minute
- **100** **minutes:** $189 per month, plus $2.09 per extra minute
- **200 minutes:** $349 per month, plus $1.99 per extra minute
- **300 minutes:** $479 per month, plus $1.89 per extra minute
- **500 minutes:** $759 per month, plus $1.79 per extra minute


The **** Live Outbound Calls **** plan unlocks features like lead outreach and appointment confirmations. Each tier depends on the number of contacts and phone numbers you call, regardless of the outcome. The PATLive agent will make up to five attempts before counting an outreach credit as spent.


Here’s what you’ll pay for each tier:


- **Pay as you go:** $19 per month, plus $8.95 per extra call
- **25 outreaches.** $199 per month, plus $8.49 per extra call
- **50 outreaches.** $309 per month, plus $8.29 per extra call
- **75 outreaches.** $459 per month, plus $7.95 per extra call
- **100 outreaches.** $599 per month plus $7.49 per extra call


You can also use one of the Live Chat plans for website visitors who need live chat support. Chats bill you on a per-session basis, and counts when either the agent or the user ends the chat. Here’s what to expect from each:


- **Pay as you go:** $19 per month, plus $9.95 per chat
- **25 chats.** $149 per month, plus $8.95 per extra chat
- **50 chats.** $279 per month, plus $8.49 per extra chat
- **75 chats.** $399 per month, plus $8.29 per extra chat
- **100 chats.** $499 per month, plus $7.95 per extra chat


### **7. 3CX AI receptionist: Best AnswerConnect alternative for multiple languages**


#### Pros


- Custom greetings
- Compatible with OpenAI or Grok
- Extended language support via OpenAI


#### Cons


- Bring Your Own AI
- Pay for your own tokens
- Three-minute call limit
- No call flow flexibility


[3CX](https://www.quo.com/blog/3cx-alternatives/) is a business phone solution with a newly released AI Receptionist. It currently has a special pricing tier, with no solo option. That means you’ll have to sign up for 3CX’s phone service to use its virtual receptionist.


The[3CX AI Receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/3cx-ai-receptionist/) is based on OpenAI. This gives it access to all of the languages that it can support. Officially, ChatGPT supports 58 languages, but user testing suggests that it’s proficient in at least 95. Apart from languages, the 3CX AI Receptionist can help:


- Route calls
- Capture leads
- Answer caller inquiries
- Take messages


Just keep in mind customers are expected to use *and* pay for their own OpenAI accounts, including tokens. Using a free or lower-tier OpenAI plan can cause performance problems with the AI Receptionist.


You should know that the AI Receptionist has a three-minute call limit, after which the caller goes to a human or your IVR. This can be abrupt for the caller and potentially lower your customer satisfaction.


### Key features of 3CX AI receptionist


**


- Call routing
- Appointment scheduling
- AI knowledge base
- Round-the-clock availability
- Customizable voice options
- Nearly 100 supported languages via OpenAI
- Automatic language switching


### 3CX AI receptionist pricing


**


3CX prices its plans based on the number of simultaneous calls you expect to field. Once you decide on a number, you’ll have to choose an Edition for that plan: Basic, Pro, or AI. The AI Receptionist is only available with the AI Edition.


For example:


- **8 simultaneous calls:** $575 per year for the AI Edition
- **16 simultaneous calls:** $1,095 per year for the AI Edition
- **24 simultaneous calls:** $1,350 per year for the AI Edition


For more specific pricing, reach out to the sales team for a quote.


##


**Why businesses are looking for AnswerConnect alternatives**


AnswerConnect’s service can help with lead capture, call routing, and after-hours phone support. But many customers experience billing and quality issues that cause them to explore other solutions.


Here are the biggest limitations of AnswerConnect:


### **Long setup**


Previous customers say that AnswerConnect can take several days to set up. The exact time depends on the:


- Complexity of your scripts
- Call handling schedules
- Integrations or workflows you need


You’ll also have to spend time training your virtual receptionists. Unfortunately, some AnswerConnect customers still report issues after training their AnswerConnect reps.


Here’s what one said after doing a few test calls:


*“When the Agents answer the call, they are not ‘engaging’ with the caller. The Agents sound very mechanized. So it’s a giveaway this is an answering service. Also, the Agents are not following the script.* ” —[Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/5d3b9658f01869069cc3db67)


### **Pricing locked behind a form**


By default, AnswerConnect locks its pricing information behind a form. That means you have to submit your contact info to see it, then prepare to be chased by the AnswerConnect sales team. After we submitted the form ourselves, we were given this pricing for reference:


- **Entry:** $350 per month plus a $49.99 setup fee for 200 minutes, basic scripting, CRM integrations, and access to the desktop and mobile apps, with $2.50 per additional minute
- **Growth:** $395 per month for 300 minutes, customizable scripting, and live chat, with $1.85 per additional minute
- **Standard:** $575 per month plus a $49.99 setup fee for 400 minutes, with $1.85 per additional minute


### **Unexpectedly high costs**


Several previous customers say they were surprised at how high their AnswerConnect bills were.


One Trustpilot[reviewer](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a5eb42015c55303f436fbfc) signed up for a $300-per-month plan but was charged over $6,000 in a week. AnswerConnect reviewed the charges and confirmed they were correct.


Another reviewer found that he was being overcharged for calls:


*“They charge by the minute, yet the actual usage—based on the start and end time of the calls—shows consistent overbilling. In many cases, calls that lasted 2 minutes and 20 seconds were rounded up to 5 minutes. The justification? “After-call work.” But this “after-call work” is untrackable, undefined, and unverifiable by the customer. It opens the door for arbitrary time inflation.”* —[TrustPilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/68c1b5df63296d62ea91353f)


### **Spam call limits**


All businesses receive spam calls of one sort or another, where a caller dials in, then hangs up after a few seconds. It could be a wrong number or it could be an automated spam call that cuts itself off. Either way, it’s not something you want to spend time or money on.


To help manage this, AnswerConnect allows for 30 free calls under 30 seconds. But anything after that will be charged as a full minute.


This has led to some nasty surprises for AnswerConnect customers. One of them was charged $85 above his $275 monthly plan just because his spam calls went above the limit. See a snippet of that here:


*“To my surprise, I was charged for 169 minutes. Over DOUBLE what was normal for our company. On the invoice, it showed that there were 131 calls. We maybe only received notification of 30 of these “calls.” After looking through every message description in the portal, I realized less than half of these “calls” had anyone on the other line, yet I was getting charged for a full minute.”* —[Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/68128f5f47b5c4f80b31fecc)


### **Agents can be hit or miss**


AnswerConnect’s agents work in a pool, where a single agent can handle several different accounts. This can reduce costs for both the customer and AnswerConnect. But it can *also* lead to account confusion and performance issues in certain situations.


Remember: you have no control over your agents. You can’t pick them, you don’t know who they are, and you don’t know how they’ve been trained. You just have to trust them to do their job properly. According to past customers, that trust can sometimes be breached.


See for yourself:


*“I had to repeatedly call callers back to correct the scheduled time or other type of problem. Oftentimes, I was spending way more time calling back clients than if I had answered the phone myself.”* —[Trustpilot](https://ca.trustpilot.com/reviews/65c1628b4dcd3c36489e5630)


##


**Try the best AnswerConnect alternative**


Answering services like AnswerConnect can help with call management, but growing businesses may find their costs and performance too unpredictable to be worth it. Their overage and after-call work tracking make it an unwise choice for businesses that need to account for every dollar and want something scalable. Their agent performance is also too inconsistent to rely on when every call matters.


That’s why Quo and Sona are the better alternative. Sona is embedded into the Quo platform, so you also get a modern business phone solution. Plus, you have clear oversight of all conversations handled by Sona in context with all other communication with your customers.


[Try Quo today with a seven-day trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) and get your first 10 Sona-handled calls for free.


##


**FAQs**


****What’s the top alternative to AnswerConnect?****


Smith.ai and AbbyConnect are decent alternatives. But we believe that Quo’s Sona is the best all-around alternative to AnswerConnect for growing businesses. You get your first 10 AI-handled calls free each month with any plan. Plus, you get a complete business phone system along with an AI receptionist you can tweak to fit your team’s needs.


****How much does AnswerConnect cost?****


AnswerConnect gates its pricing behind a contact form, but the plans are priced as follows:
**– Entry:** $350 per month plus a $49.99 setup fee
**– Growth:** $395 per month with no setup fee

****Does AnswerConnect use an AI receptionist?****
